sw.R: Watu kadhaa walimletea Yesu mtu mmoja. Mtu huyo hakuweza kusikia, na aliweza kuongea kwa shida sana. Wakamwomba Yesu aweke mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} juu ya mtu huyo na kumponya.

decisions.choice: speaking with difficulty: hardly able to speak
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It may mean a stammer or near silence. In 7:37 the crowd call such people mute.

decisions.choice: deaf and hardly able to speak: Isaiah 35:5-6
decisions.reason: The same rare word is used in the Greek translation of Isaiah 35:6, where the deaf will hear and the tongue of the mute will sing when God comes to save.

decisions.choice: bring, beg: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: and heal him
decisions.reason: Readable says why they asked him to lay on his hand (5:23).

source.text: καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου κατ’ ἰδίαν ἔβαλεν τοὺς δακτύλους αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εφφαθα, ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι·

records.literal_gloss: And having taken him away from the crowd privately he put the fingers of him into the ears of him and having spit he touched the tongue of him, \v 34 and having looked up to the heaven he sighed and says to him, Ephphatha, which is, Be opened.

en.L: And taking him aside from the crowd privately, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fingers into his ears, and spitting, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched his tongue; \v 34 and looking up to heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sighed deeply and says to him, "Ephphatha," which is, "Be opened."
en.B: Jesus led him off from the crowd to be alone with him. He pushed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fingers into the man's ears, spat, and touched his tongue. \v 34 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up to heaven, groaned, and said to him, "Ephphatha," meaning, "Be opened."
en.R: Jesus took the man away from the crowd, to a place where they could be alone. He put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fingers in the man's ears. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spat and touched the man's tongue. \v 34 Jesus looked up toward heaven and let out a deep sigh. He said to the man, "Ephphatha!" This word means "Be opened!"

es.L: Y apartándolo de la multitud, a solas, le metió {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} dedos en los oídos y, escupiendo, le tocó la lengua; \v 34 y levantando los ojos al cielo, suspiró profundamente y le dice: «Efatá», que es: «Sé abierto».
es.B: Jesús lo llevó aparte, lejos de la multitud, para estar a solas con él. Le metió {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} dedos en los oídos, escupió y le tocó la lengua. \v 34 Luego miró al cielo, gimió y le dijo: «Efatá», que significa «Ábrete».
es.R: Jesús se llevó al hombre lejos de la multitud, a un lugar donde pudieran estar solos. Le puso {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} dedos en los oídos. Luego escupió y le tocó la lengua. \v 34 Jesús miró hacia el cielo y dio un profundo suspiro. Le dijo al hombre: «¡Efatá!». Esta palabra quiere decir «¡Ábrete!».

sw.L: Naye alimchukua kando mbali na umati, faraghani, akatia vidole {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} masikioni mwake, na akiisha kutema mate, akaugusa ulimi wake; \v 34 na akitazama juu mbinguni, akapiga kite, na anamwambia, "Efatha," yaani, "Funguka."
sw.B: Yesu alimchukua kando, mbali na umati, ili wawe peke yao. Akatia vidole {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} masikioni mwa mtu huyo, akatema mate, akaugusa ulimi wake. \v 34 Kisha akatazama juu mbinguni, akapiga kite, akamwambia, "Efatha," maana yake, "Funguka."
sw.R: Yesu alimchukua mtu huyo mbali na umati, mahali ambapo wangeweza kuwa peke yao. Akatia vidole {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}} masikioni mwa mtu huyo. Kisha akatema mate, akaugusa ulimi wa mtu huyo. \v 34 Yesu alitazama juu mbinguni, akapiga kite. Akamwambia mtu huyo, "Efatha!" Neno hili maana yake ni "Funguka!"

decisions.choice: fingers in the ears, spit on the tongue: signs a deaf man could feel and see
decisions.reason: Spittle was widely thought to have healing power. Jesus shows by touch what he is about to do for the ears and the tongue (compare 8:23).

decisions.choice: looking up to heaven: turning to God in prayer
decisions.reason: Jesus looks up before he blesses the bread in 6:41.

decisions.choice: sighed deeply: groaned, with deep feeling
decisions.reason: The groan may be prayer, or grief at the suffering caused by sickness (compare Romans 8:22-23).

decisions.choice: Ephphatha: an Aramaic word, kept and translated by Mark
decisions.reason: As with Talitha koum (5:41), Mark keeps Jesus' own word and translates it for Greek readers.

decisions.choice: says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: Ephphatha, written in English letters
decisions.reason: All levels keep the Aramaic word as Mark does, since he translates it himself.

decisions.choice: Efatha, in Swahili letters
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the Aramaic word and translates it (meaning decision m4), and so do these drafts. Swahili spells it as it is said, as the English writes it in English letters.

decisions.choice: akapiga kite
decisions.reason: The verb is a deep sigh or groan (meaning decision m3, uncertain). "Kupiga kite" is to sigh deeply; "kuugua" can also mean to fall ill, which would mislead.

decisions.choice: Efatá, in Spanish spelling
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the Aramaic word and translates it (meaning decision m4), and so do these drafts. Spanish writes it as it is pronounced in Spanish, with the stress mark, as the English writes it in English letters.

source.text: καὶ ἠνοίγησαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί, καὶ ἐλύθη ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς·

records.literal_gloss: And were opened of him the hearings, and was loosed the bond of the tongue of him, and he was speaking rightly.

en.L: And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he began speaking plainly.
en.B: His ears were opened, his tongue was set free from what bound it, and he spoke clearly.
en.R: Then the man's ears were opened, and he could hear. His tongue was set free, and he could talk clearly.

es.L: Y se le abrieron los oídos, y se soltó la atadura de su lengua, y hablaba correctamente.
es.B: Se le abrieron los oídos, su lengua quedó libre de lo que la ataba, y hablaba con claridad.
es.R: Entonces los oídos del hombre se abrieron, y pudo oír. Su lengua quedó libre, y pudo hablar con claridad.

sw.L: Na yakafunguliwa masikio yake, na kikafunguliwa kifungo cha ulimi wake, naye akawa anaongea sawasawa.
sw.B: Masikio yake yalifunguliwa, ulimi wake ukawekwa huru kutoka kwa kile kilichoufunga, naye akaongea waziwazi.
sw.R: Basi masikio ya mtu huyo yakafunguka, akaweza kusikia. Ulimi wake ukawa huru, akaweza kuongea vizuri.

decisions.choice: hearings: the ears, the organs of hearing
decisions.reason: The plural word for hearing is used for the ears.

decisions.choice: the bond of his tongue was loosed: what held his tongue was taken away
alternatives: a bond put on him by an evil power
decisions.reason: The words picture the tongue as tied. Some see a binding by Satan, as in Luke 13:16, but Mark speaks of no demon here.

decisions.choice: were opened, without "immediately", the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "immediately", a word Mark often uses. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: he began speaking: the imperfect, he went on speaking
decisions.reason: He began to speak and kept on.

source.text: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν· ὅσον δὲ αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο, αὐτοὶ μᾶλλον περισσότερον ἐκήρυσσον.

records.literal_gloss: And he ordered them that no one they should tell; as much as but he them was ordering, they more even more were proclaiming.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them to tell no one; but the more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them, the more abundantly they themselves were proclaiming [it].
en.B: Jesus told them to say nothing to anyone. Yet the more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave this order, the more eagerly they spread the news.
en.R: Jesus told the people not to tell anyone about this. But the more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them not to, the more they told others about it.

es.L: Y les ordenó que no lo dijeran a nadie; pero cuanto más se lo ordenaba, tanto más ellos mismos lo proclamaban.
es.B: Jesús les mandó que no se lo contaran a nadie. Pero cuanto más se lo mandaba, con más empeño difundían la noticia.
es.R: Jesús les dijo a las personas que no se lo contaran a nadie. Pero cuanto más se lo decía, más se lo contaban a otros.

sw.L: Na aliwaamuru wasimwambie mtu yeyote; lakini kwa kadiri alivyokuwa akiwaamuru, wao wenyewe walizidi sana kulitangaza [jambo hilo].
sw.B: Yesu aliwaonya wasimwambie mtu yeyote. Lakini kadiri alivyotoa agizo hilo, ndivyo walivyoeneza habari kwa bidii zaidi.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia watu wasimwambie mtu yeyote habari hii. Lakini kadiri alivyowakataza, ndivyo walivyozidi kuwaambia wengine.

decisions.choice: the command to tell no one: Jesus does not want fame as a wonder-worker
decisions.reason: As in 1:44 and 5:43, Jesus orders silence. Here the order is broken, as in 1:45.

decisions.choice: proclaiming: making known in public
decisions.reason: The verb is used for preaching (1:14, 1:45). They spread the news everywhere.

decisions.choice: the more ... the more: the people do the very opposite of the order
decisions.reason: The comparatives are doubled for stress.

decisions.choice: them: the people who brought the man (7:32)
decisions.reason: Those ordered are those who brought the man and saw him healed.

source.text: καὶ ὑπερπερισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Καλῶς πάντα πεποίηκεν, καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ποιεῖ ἀκούειν καὶ ἀλάλους λαλεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And beyond measure they were astonished, saying, Well all things he has done, and the deaf he makes to hear and the mute to speak.

en.L: And they were astonished beyond measure, saying, "He has done all things well; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes both the deaf to hear and the mute to speak."
en.B: The people were utterly astounded. "How well {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done everything!" they said. "He gives hearing to the deaf and speech to those who cannot talk!"
en.R: The people were completely amazed. They said, "Everything Jesus does is good! He even makes deaf people able to hear, and people who cannot talk able to speak!"

es.L: Y se asombraban sobremanera, diciendo: «Todo lo ha hecho bien; hace que tanto los sordos oigan como los mudos hablen».
es.B: La gente estaba asombradísima, y decía: «¡Qué bien lo ha hecho todo! ¡A los sordos les da el oído, y a los que no pueden hablar, el habla!».
es.R: La gente estaba completamente maravillada. Decían: «¡Todo lo que hace Jesús es bueno! ¡Hasta hace que los sordos oigan y que los mudos hablen!».

sw.L: Na walistaajabu mno kupita kipimo, wakisema, "Kila kitu amekifanya vizuri; hata viziwi anawawezesha kusikia na bubu kuongea."
sw.B: Watu walishangaa kabisa. Walisema, "Ni vizuri namna gani alivyofanya kila kitu! Anawapa viziwi uwezo wa kusikia, na wasioweza kuongea uwezo wa kuongea!"
sw.R: Watu walishangaa sana. Wakasema, "Kila kitu ambacho Yesu anafanya ni kizuri! Hata anawafanya viziwi waweze kusikia, na wasioweza kuongea waweze kuongea!"

decisions.choice: the deaf hear and the mute speak: Isaiah 35:5-6
decisions.reason: Isaiah promised that when God comes to save, the ears of the deaf will be opened and the mute will sing. The crowd's words echo that promise.

decisions.choice: he has done all things well: perhaps an echo of Genesis 1:31
decisions.reason: In Genesis God saw all that he had made and it was very good. The words may also be only an exclamation of praise.

decisions.choice: beyond measure: completely, past all bounds
decisions.reason: Mark uses a strong word found only here in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: the deaf, the mute: people of this kind, not only this man
decisions.reason: The plural speaks in general of what Jesus does.

decisions.choice: How well he has done everything (B); Everything Jesus does is good (R)
alternatives: he has done all things well
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable shape the praise as natural speech.
